passage:
A small doorbell was placed on the counter of a family restaurant. Customers could ring it if no worker was there.
At first, children rang it for fun. The sound became annoying. The owner wanted to remove it.
Then his daughter made a sign: "Please ring once. We are cooking for you."
After the sign appeared, most people stopped playing with the bell. They understood that workers were busy, not ignoring them.
The owner kept the bell.
The daughter learned that signs do more than tell people what to do. A good sign explains the situation. When people understand the reason, they often behave better.
